continuation_seam_observed: 3.1 At any turning state choose orthonormal axes $e_1=x/r_*$ and $e_2=p/|p|$, and translate its time to $0$; then $x=r_*e_1$ and $p=(J/r_*)e_2$. The root equation in 2.1 gives $H(x,p)=W$, and the smooth field in [F1] satisfies [F2], giving a local solution. By [F2], all solutions through this full initial state agree on their overlapping intervals; their union is a solution on the union interval, is locally a solution near every interior point, and is the unique maximal extension. Its interval is open, since local existence at an included finite endpoint would extend it. Every trajectory through the state is a restriction of this extension by uniqueness. Along it, direct differentiation gives $\dot p_r=c^2J^2/(\mathcal E r^3)+\kappa/r^2>0$ everywhere, so [F5] makes $p_r$ strictly increasing with its unique zero at $0$; consequently $r$ decreases before the turn and increases after it. On every allowed state $0<u\le u_*<(W-mc^2)/\kappa$, hence $r\ge r_*$ and $mc^2<\mathcal E=W-\kappa u<W$, which gives $|p|<\sqrt A$. Also $|\dot x|<c$, so near any finite interval endpoint $x$ remains bounded and $|x|\ge r_*$; together with the momentum bound this gives compact containment in $D$. Applying [F2] at a finite right endpoint, or to the reversed-time field at a finite left endpoint, would properly extend the maximal solution, a contradiction. Its interval is therefore $\mathbb R$. Each monotone radial tail must be unbounded: if it had a finite limit greater than $r_*$, then $Q(1/r)$ and $\mathcal E$ would give $|\dot r|$ a positive lower bound, contradicting that finite limit. Thus $r\to\infty$ on both tails and $\dot r=c^2p_r/\mathcal E\to\pm c^2\sqrt A/W$, so $r$ grows linearly there. Then $|\dot p|=\kappa/r^2$ is integrable, and $p$ converges to incoming and outgoing limits of magnitude $\sqrt A$. Since the tangential momentum has magnitude $J/r\to0$, the limiting momenta point along the limiting radial directions, giving the two asymptotic velocity directions.
